acceptance_criteria: AC-1 D2 entity applicability producer: pure function(s) deriving, per (entity, capability), one of APPLICABLE / NOT_APPLICABLE / APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN from the entity's logical type (physical member, VSX virtual system, cluster, Panorama-managed device, etc.) and each capability's declared applicable-entity-type set. The declared set is read from a single, explicit, closed table this movement adds (not inferred from naming, vendor guesses, or capability id substrings) -- cite the exact source for each entry or mark it UNKNOWN rather than guess.

AC-2 D3 vendor/platform support producer: pure function(s) deriving SUPPORTED / UNSUPPORTED / SUPPORT_UNKNOWN per (vendor/platform, capability) from positive evidence only -- section 7.3's rule (grep the contract yourself: what may and may not prove capability support) governs; a missing/absent producer, a failed collection, or an unrecognized platform must never be read as UNSUPPORTED, only as SUPPORT_UNKNOWN.

AC-3 both producers are pure, offline, no device/network/registry I/O -- callers (the M10.2 resolver, once wired, out of this movement's scope) supply the typed inputs (entity kind, vendor/platform, capability id); this movement does not import or extend utils/capability_registry.py (the distinct 0.6.1C collection-capability planner named as a namespace-collision risk in M10.1's own history) and does not wire anything into html_export, console, payloads, or navigation.

AC-4 vocabulary discipline: output values match docs/design/CAPABILITY_STATE_VOCABULARY_AND_PRESENTATION.md section 4 exactly (APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN, SUPPORT_UNKNOWN as named there); a test asserts these tokens are disjoint from the job lifecycle (X1), the OP.2 action-state set (X2), and utils.action_taxonomy -- mirroring M10.1's own AC-8 precedent.

AC-5 evidence and closed sources: the entity-type table (AC-1) and the vendor/platform support table (AC-2) each cite their real source (an existing repository module, a frozen contract section, or an explicit vendor documentation reference) per entry; no entry is invented from plausible-sounding vendor knowledge -- if a genuine gap exists, the entry is SUPPORT_UNKNOWN/APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN with the gap named, not filled by guessing.

AC-6 validation and state: targeted test module green; tests/test_architecture_convergence.py unchanged and green; project-state bookkeeping in this PR. This movement runs in parallel with M10.2, GOV.PO.3, OP.1 and a small backlog-fix bundle, each in its own worktree: merge origin/main before opening/merging your PR and resolve any mechanical bookkeeping conflicts yourself.

baseline.sequencing: Third M10 slice, authorized 2026-09-08 alongside M10.2 -- the two are independent (M10.2 is resolver logic over typed inputs; M10.3 produces two of those input dimensions) and run concurrently in separate worktrees, not sequentially.

context_not_loaded: console, templates/static, OP.x, vendor collector internals beyond what AC-1/AC-2 need to cite
invariants: Positive-evidence-only support proof (section 7.3) -- absence, failure, or an unrecognized platform is never read as UNSUPPORTED
No coercion/inference to fill a genuine gap -- UNKNOWN with a named reason is always the correct answer over a guess
Pure functions only; no I/O, no device contact, no new collector

entries.text: Implemented AC-1..AC-6: new utils/capability_applicability.py (resolve_d2) and utils/capability_vendor_support.py (resolve_d3) -- pure, offline, closed-table producers for CAPABILITY_STATE_VOCABULARY_AND_PRESENTATION.md section 3.3's D2 (APPLICABLE/NOT_APPLICABLE/APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN, from NAVIGATION_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2's eight logical entity types) and D3 (SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/SUPPORT_UNKNOWN, from real repository collector/adapter evidence). Every APPLICABLE/NOT_APPLICABLE/SUPPORTED entry cites its exact source; every uncited pair resolves the UNKNOWN value naming the gap, never a guess (section 7.3, section 8.2 point 1). No UNSUPPORTED entry populated -- no citable positive evidence of vendor non-support found for any of the seven PCP.0 capabilities; utils/operate/adapter.py (D3's own cited input for controlled_operations) carries zero concrete vendor adapter, and no telemetry/diagnostics producer exists anywhere -- both treated as absent-producer SUPPORT_UNKNOWN per section 8.2 point 1, not UNSUPPORTED, correcting PRODUCT_CONTROL_PLANE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 8's own informal worked-example wording. Neither module imports or extends utils/capability_registry.py; no resolver/UI/navigation/payload wiring (M10.2's job). tests/test_m10_3_entity_and_vendor_support_producers.py: 107 passed, including vocabulary-separation against the job lifecycle/OP.2 action-state/action-taxonomy tokens (AC-4, mirroring M10.1's AC-8 precedent) and D2/D3 mutual disjointness. tests/test_architecture_convergence.py: 22 passed, unchanged. utils.project_plan.build_project_plan_payload()['metadata_warnings'] == []. git diff --check clean. Repository privacy gate (main.py --repository-privacy-check): FAIL/3 pre-existing findings only, identical to origin/main before this branch and to PR #127/#129's own evidence -- none introduced by this movement. origin/main merged into this branch before opening the PR (reconciled build_history.json/roadmap.json/CURRENT_STATE.md/docs/history/INDEX.md against the concurrently-merged gov_po_3_orchestrator_observability, PR #129).
